 Pei Jing proud of pushing limits at 34 with Pang Ron despite missing Finals ticket
 By T. RAHULESH 
 Saturday, 21 Nov 2026
 | 5:10 PM MYT
 share 
 bookmark 
 Pride beyond results: Hoo Pang Ron-Lai Pei Jing climbed to 14th in the World Tour Finals qualification standings despite the financial burden of competing as an independent pair. — IZZRAFIQ ALIAS/The Star 
 PETALING JAYA: Most athletes see a steep decline in performance once they hit their thirties.
 At 34, independent mixed doubles shuttler Lai Pei Jing wanted to put this to the test to find out how far she could still push herself.
 Seven tournaments in seven weeks with Hoo Pang Ron gave her an answer she could be proud of.
 "I was tired, but I wanted to see how far I could push myself at 34," said Pei Jing after their second round exit at the Hong Kong Open.
 "We were so close. Maybe it was one more match, one more win.
 "Of course there’s some regret, but I’m proud of myself and my partner."
 The loss to China’s world No. 2 Jiang Zhenbang-Wei Yaxin at the Kai Tai Arena meant that their bid for qualification to the season-ending World Tour Finals ended.
 A Finals berth had looked a distant prospect at the start of September, when Pang Ron-Pei Jing were 36th in the qualification standings.
 The pair climbed to 14th by the start of the Hong Kong Open after finishing runners-up at the China and French Open, reaching the semi-finals of the Denmark and Hylo Opens and making the Korean Open quarter-finals.
 The pair managed this against all odds especially with the financial burden of being an independent pairing resulting in them having to manage their own recovery through four weeks in Europe and three in Asia.
 "We got through seven tournaments in a row without pain or injury, even without a travelling physiotherapist.”
 "When we didn’t have a coach with us, we worked things out together. It feels good to have each other’s support," added Pei Jing.
 For Pei Jing, whose last title came at the 2022 Korean Open with then partner Tan Kian Meng, standing on the podium again in France was another reason to celebrate.
 The pair had already exceeded her goal of breaking into the world’s top 32.
 Pang Ron, in a post on his social media, added that he was also battling sickness on tour.
 "I even fell sick while travelling from Germany to Korea, with the flu, cough and fever," he said.
 "We know how much hard work and sacrifice it took to get here, and we should be proud of ourselves."
 The pair can now take a break before the new World Tour season opens with the Super 1000 Malaysian Open from Jan 21-31 in Kuala Lumpur.
 Their entry has yet to be confirmed.
